newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. carrier Enterprise steams toward Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. carrier Enterprise steams toward Gulf.

text.p: The U.S. aircraft carrier Enterprise steamed out of the Suez Canal and towards the Gulf on Sunday loaded with attack aircraft to join a U.S. military build-up against Iraq.

"We are moving because our President (Bill Clinton) dialled 911..." the carrier's commanding officer Captain Michael Malone said, referring to a phone number used by citizens in the U.S. in emergencies.
"The navy is answering the call by repositioning this aircraft carrier," he said in a telephone interview from the carrier, heading south in the Red Sea late on Sunday.
"We are transiting at the best speed we can make. If tasked, we could be within striking distance of Iraq in just a couple of days," Malone told Reuters.

Tensions between the United States and Iraq soared last week over Baghdad's threats to attack U.S. and allied air patrols in a no-fly zone in its territory, and after Washington launched 44 cruise missiles into southern Iraq.
Iraq has since said it was suspending the threat.
The United States boosted its military muscle in the region by sending four B-52 bombers to the Indian Ocean island of Diego Garcia and eight Stealth fighter-bombers to Kuwait.
The nuclear-powered Enterprise is the second U.S. carrier in the region.
Malone declined to give details about its final destination or mission. But he said the Enterprise, which has 74 planes, was the first to carry an enhanced F-14 fighter capability.
It was redeployed from the Adriatic, where it was sent in June with the 14 F-14s modified for laser-guided bombs.
"We are the first air wing to deploy with this capability," Malone said. "I mean ever in history. This is a new capability and we are the first air wing to take it to sea."
"The F-14...is now capable as an air-to-air and air-to-ground airplane. So it multiplies the force that we carry on the carrier," Malone said.
A supply ship and cruiser were accompanying the carrier, he said.
